newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on lower-priced competitors.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on lower-priced competitors.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower and new contract lows were set as the market remains plagued by steep U.S. wheat prices relative to other wheat-producing countries, traders said.
"Wheat can't rally at these levels, we could break a dime and still be overpriced compared with other countries," a trader said.
The new contract low for March was $3.94 per bushel, below the previous low of $3.99-1/2 set Thursday.
Wheat dropped despite a bigger-than-expected number in USDA's weekly export sales report.
USDA early Friday said U.S. wheat exports during the week ended October 10 totaled 737,000 tonnes, more than double the previous week and 75 percent above the four-week average.
Technicians said before the open Friday, the four- and 20-day moving averages were giving off bearish signals.
First resistance for December was at $4.16 per bushel and second resistance was at $4.24-1/2. The session high for December was $4.13. First support was at $4.07-1/2 and second support at $3.99.
Wheat closed three to 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 6-1/4 at $4.04-3/4.
Fund selling led the way down with Smith Barney a key seller of two million bushels of December and Dean Witter Reynolds also sold two million December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, down from 21,751 Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Smith Barney bought 1,500 March $4.80 calls at 1-1/2 cents and FIMAT Futures bought 1,50 March $4.80 calls at 1-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 15,000 contracts, up from 6,190 Thursday.
